Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

# Test skill: run_tests.py reports a retry-accepted stage as FAIL (exit 0, `outcome=retry-clean`)

## Problem statement

`scripts/run_tests.py` (the shared test skill) harvests failure names from a
stage's **combined output** (`parse_failures`) even when the stage's own retry
runner (`vitest-run-with-retry.ts`) already discarded the failing attempt and
returned **exit 0**. A `retry-clean` stage is therefore reported as a suite
failure and the dev→main release gate blocks a genuinely green tree — observed
during the v0.1.24 release of Tableau-Card-Engine (merged tree, load ~7).

## Users

- **Release engineer** (primary): runs the ship skill's release gate
  (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` → `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`).
  User story: "As a release engineer, I want a stage the project's own retry
  runner already accepted (`outcome=retry-clean` / `accepted-transient`) to be
  reported green, so a contention flake the runner already recovered from does
  not block a release whose code is sound."
- **Audit consumers**: `audit_runner.py` shares `parse_failures` for F-cache
  misses; its verdicts should classify the same way (green after accepted
  retry, never `unparsed_failure`).
- **Operators triaging a red run**: want to see *which file flaked* on the
  discarded attempt as diagnostics, not as a suite failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a command's output carries the retry runner's final green verdict
      (`[vitest-runner] ... status=0 outcome=retry-clean` or
      `status=0 outcome=accepted-transient`), `parse_failures` discards the
      failure names harvested from the superseded attempt and the suite
      reports success (`success=True`, `failures=[]`).
- [ ] The masking guards are unchanged: a stage whose retry ends
      `outcome=retry-failed` / `outcome=failed` (or any non-zero `status` on
      the runner line), or a stage with **no** retry banner, still reports
      every genuine failure (per-stage segmentation: only failures from
      green-verdict stages are discarded, so a retry-clean browser stage never
      masks a genuine unit/tutorial failure in the same `npm test` output).
- [ ] The discarded-attempt failures remain visible as diagnostics (not as
      suite failures) — e.g. a notice/`notice_code` naming the flaked file
      and/or a structured JSON field on the suite result — so an operator can
      still see which file flaked.
- [ ] Unit tests (SorraAgents `skill/test/tests/`) cover: (a) retry-clean
      output with a failed first attempt → green; (b) retry-failed output →
      red with the failures listed; (c) genuine-failure-only output (no
      banner / no retry) → red, unchanged; (d) mixed output where only the
      green-verdict stage's failures are discarded.
- [ ] The release gate (`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` →
      `run_tests.py --scope full`) no longer needs a re-run after an accepted
      retry, verified with the captured cache entry
      (`.worklog/cache/ce0b22f933c88660bc44ee97bca48193`) replaying green.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the change — module and
      function docstrings in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (the
      `parse_failures`/`parse_vitest_failures` contract) and any
      `docs/dev/*` pages that enumerate failure classification/outcomes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes (SorraAgents:
      `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full` from the
      SorraAgents repo — the shared-skill suite; neither repo's suite is
      degraded by the parser change). CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.

## Impact

A release whose browser stage flaked once and was recovered by the retry runner
now passes the gate on the first run instead of forcing the operator to
re-run the full suite to prove a green tree.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repo boundary (assumption):** the change is made in the SorraAgents
  checkout where the code is versioned; this CG item records it. If the
  producer prefers a WL mirror item, planning may create it — the code change
  is identical either way (see Constraints *tracking decision*).
- **Additive result fields only:** surfacing discarded failures must be
  additive (`discarded_failures`/notice), never remove or rename existing
  suite/aggregate result keys consumers (`run_cached` metadata, audit, ship
  gate) rely on.
- **Shared-parser regression risk:** `parse_failures` is consumed by the audit
  too; AC7 (full suite) and the unchanged-path unit tests guard this. A
  mis-parsed verdict only ever *keeps* failures (red), never drops a genuine
  one — fail-safe direction.
- **Scope creep:** per-stage JSON diagnostics, cache-format changes, or
  altering the retry runner are out of scope; any follow-ups become linked
  work items, not part of this fix.

## Constraints

- **Code location is the shared agent-framework repo, not this repo.** The
  canonical `run_tests.py` lives at
  `SorraAgents/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (symlinked into
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`); it is NOT tracked in
  Tableau-Card-Engine. Tests live in `SorraAgents/skill/test/tests/`
  (`test_run_tests_vitest_parser.py` is the primary target for parser unit
  tests). Implementation therefore happens in the SorraAgents checkout, whose
  own repo gates (build → test → commit; `dev`-only pushes) apply. **Tracking
  decision (assumption, flag for producer):** this CG item stays the tracker
  here; the cross-repo change is recorded on it per the repo-boundary rules
  (never edit `.pi/`/`skill/` trees from TCE unless explicitly instructed —
  this item IS the explicit instruction for `run_tests.py`). If the producer
  prefers a SorraAgents `WL` mirror item, that may be created at planning; the
  code change itself is identical.
- **Do not change the retry runner's semantics.** The fix is in the
  *consumer* (`parse_failures`); `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` already guarantees
  `retry-clean` means the second attempt passed and `accepted-transient` means
  every error block was attributable to an acceptable transient signature.
- **Token name:** the ACs' "transient-accepted" corrects to the runner's
  actual token `outcome=accepted-transient` (emitted by
  `vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, `runSummary(..., 'accepted-transient', ...)`).
  Both green tokens (`retry-clean`, `accepted-transient`) must be honoured;
  `status=0` must accompany them.
- **Multiple runner lines:** `npm --silent test` runs several stages; each
  retry-runner stage emits its own `[vitest-runner]` line. Green verdicts must
  be attributed per stage/segment so a genuine failure elsewhere in the same
  command is never masked.
- **Shared consumers:** `parse_failures` is imported by both
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (`run_suite`) and
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`; both must classify consistently.
- **Fixture evidence:** the exact output shape is captured at
  `Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/cache/ce0b22f933c88660bc44ee97bca48193/`
  (unit `outcome=clean`, browser FAIL block, `[retry]` banner, browser
  `outcome=retry-clean`, exit 0) and `/tmp/ship-release-20261113-042438.log`.

## Existing state

- `run_tests.py` (shared test skill) routes Vitest output into
  `parse_vitest_failures` (MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS); Vitest browser output like
  `FAIL |browser (chromium)|
  tests/core-engine/tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts` parses into a
  structured record from the `Failed Tests` block.
- The retry runner (`Tableau-Card-Engine/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`)
  emits a final machine-readable
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=N status=S outcome=... expected=N ran=M` line to
  stderr after every attempt sequence (outcomes: `clean`, `failed`,
  `retry-clean`, `retry-failed`, `accepted-transient`, `coverage-failed`,
  `hang`).
- `run_suite` builds `success = overall_returncode == 0 and not all_failures`;
  on the v0.1.24 run `npm --silent test` exited 0 but `all_failures` contained
  the browser file parsed from the superseded first attempt → stage reported
  `FAIL ... exit_code=0` and the release needed a re-run.
- `run_tests.py` currently treats the `[vitest-runner]` line only as a block
  terminator in the Vitest parser (`_VITEST_BLOCK_END_RE`); it never inspects
  the verdict.

## Desired change

- In the shared failure-parsing entry point (`parse_failures`), segment the
  command output by the runner's `[vitest-runner]` verdict lines. For a
  segment whose verdict is `status=0` + (`retry-clean` | `accepted-transient`),
  harvest the failures from that stage so they can be reported as discarded
  diagnostics, but return no suite-failure records from it. Segments with a
  non-green verdict (any non-zero `status`, or no banner at all) keep the
  current behaviour — every genuine failure is reported.
- Preserve the discarded names as diagnostics: a notice/`notice_code` (and/or
  a structured field on the suite result, e.g. `discarded_failures`) naming
  the flaked file(s), so an operator can see what the retry recovered.
- Keep the route shared: because the change lives in `parse_failures`, the
  audit's failure harvesting classifies identically.
- Land with unit tests in `skill/test/tests/` covering green/red/unchanged
  paths including a mixed-output case; replay the captured cache entry as the
  canonical retry-clean fixture.

## Key Files

- `SorraAgents/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `parse_failures`,
  `parse_vitest_failures`, `run_suite` (`_result`/`success`), `run_all`
  (aggregate failures/notices) — add the retry-verdict discard + diagnostics.
- `SorraAgents/skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_vitest_parser.py` — parser unit
  tests (existing fixture-driven coverage for FAIL blocks, trees, frames).
- `SorraAgents/skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` /
  `test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` — suite-level/notice coverage for the
  diagnostics field if the implementation surfaces one.
- `SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — shared consumer; verify
  (no change expected) that its failure harvesting classifies retry-clean as
  green.
- `Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/cache/ce0b22f933c88660bc44ee97bca48193/`
  (stdout.txt + metadata.json exit_code 0) — canonical retry-clean fixture.
- `Tableau-Card-Engine/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — reference for the
  runner verdict contract (read-only; do not change).
- `SorraAgents/skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — the release
  gate that consumes the verdict (AC5 verification point; no change expected).

## Related work

- `SorraAgents/Skill` items (WL):
  - SA-0MW3GCRWE0061VDW — "Test skill: aggregate state_changed_during_run
    notice and drop failures" — the direct precedent: a flagged command's
    parsed failures are dropped from suite/aggregate and surfaced as a
    stable notice; this item follows the same pattern for the retry verdict
    (see the `state_changed_flag` short-circuit in `run_suite`).
  - SA-0MSAC1BIP004IQ3T / SA-0MSAC1BG6000Z1CM — run_tests.py runner + tests.
  - MS-0MW3UR8SX009YZWS — Vitest failure parsing (the FAIL-block parser this
    fix extends).
  - Duplicate check performed (wl search terms: "retry-clean",
    "parse_failures retry", "release gate retry stage", plus completed-item
    search) — no overlapping completed or open item found; this CG item is the
    only tracker for the parser-side discard.
- `Tableau-Card-Engine` items (CG):
  - CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3 / CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE / CG-0MVNDK56G007C1U7 /
    CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N / CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F / CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU /
    CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H — the contention-signature retry work in
    `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` whose outcome tokens this fix consumes.
  - CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09 — "Release gate: unit-stage 300s hang bound aborts
    full-suite runs on a contended host" (open; related release-gate
    robustness concern, not a duplicate — different stage/verdict).

## Related work (automated report)

- **CG-0MU4U38HU000AXU2** — [test-failure] `<suite exited 1>: npm --silent
  test — failing test` (completed) — retry-attributable failure surfaced by
  the same `npm test` command shape.
- **CG-0MQ1HJIL8000EPKV** — [Test] HUD Layer Contract Tests (completed).
- **CG-0MQN0TW5M000ADLL** — F3: DurationEventCard type & tests (completed).
- Repository matches: `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`
  (keyword overlap only; no code overlap).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The code change lives in the SorraAgents repo (shared skill) while this
  item is CG-tracked in Tableau-Card-Engine — should the work be implemented
  from this CG item (cross-repo, recorded here) or mirrored as a SorraAgents
  WL item?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (recorded for the producer; the brief assumes
  the former with the code change being identical either way). Answering party:
  producer at review/plan. Research: `run_tests.py` resolves to
  `SorraAgents/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (verified via
  `readlink -f`/inode); TCE has no copy; the release gate lives in
  `SorraAgents/skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`; SA-0MW3GCRWE0061VDW
  is the same script fixed from a WL item.
- Q: "The AC wording 'transient-accepted' — the runner actually emits
  `accepted-transient`." — Answer (agent, from source):
  `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` emits `outcome=accepted-transient`
  (`runSummary(..., 'accepted-transient', ...)`); the AC text above uses
  `accepted-transient`. Source: source code is more authoritative than the
  work item; no user confirmation needed.
- No further interview questions: the seed context (evidence section, cache
  entry, release log) sufficed to draft the brief; no answers were required to
  proceed.
